facts.fact_text: From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the protest rallies from 20 February 2008 onwards was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
The applicant was a member of the political council of an opposition party.
The applicant was a supporter of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's candidacy at the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election.
The applicant was an active participant in the protest rallies, regularly attending the ongoing demonstrations and sit-ins at Freedom Square.
According to the applicant, on 24 February 2008 at around 10 a.m. he and two of his friends, A.Sis. and V.K., were driving home from the rally at Freedom Square.
According to the applicant, on 24 February 2008 at around 10 a.m. the car in which the applicant, A.Sis. and V.K. were travelling was blocked on Teryan Street in Yerevan by another car.
According to the applicant, masked gunmen emerged from the blocking car and demanded that the applicant and his friends get out of their car.

According to the applicant, he and his companions A.Sis. and V.K. were forced into the blocking car and taken to the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime of the Armenian Police (PDFOC).

According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime of the Armenian Police (PDFOC) on 24 February 2008 at around 11.30 a.m. by operative police officers of the PDFOC.
On 25 February 2008 the investigator decided to institute a criminal case under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (non-life or health-threatening assault on a public official).
On 27 February 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan decided to allow the investigator's application for the applicant's detention, finding that, if the applicant remained at large, he could commit a new offence, abscond or obstruct the investigation.
On 19 November 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant guilty as charged.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code to two years' imprisonment.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code to a fine in the amount of 300,000 Armenian drams (AMD).

On 27 February 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The decision formally charging the applicant stated that on 24 February 2008 at around 11.30 p.m. in front of Kentron Police Station the applicant had threatened the police officers and, in defiance of their lawful orders, inflicted non-life-threatening violence on police officer K.H. by punching him in the chest.
On 19 November 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant guilty as charged.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code to two years' imprisonment.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code to a fine in the amount of 300,000 Armenian drams (AMD).
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the protest rallies from 20 February 2008 onwards was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
The applicant was a supporter of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's candidacy at the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election.
The applicant was an active participant in the protest rallies, regularly attending the ongoing demonstrations and sit-ins at Freedom Square.
According to the applicant, on 24 February 2008 at around 10 a.m. he and two of his friends, A.Sis. and V.K., were driving home from the rally at Freedom Square.
According to the applicant, on 24 February 2008 at around 10 a.m. the car in which the applicant, A.Sis. and V.K. were travelling was blocked on Teryan Street in Yerevan by another car.
According to the applicant, masked gunmen emerged from the blocking car and demanded that the applicant and his friends get out of their car.
According to the applicant, he was thrown to the ground and searched but nothing was found.

According to the applicant, he and his companions A.Sis. and V.K. were forced into the blocking car and taken to the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime of the Armenian Police (PDFOC).

The applicant, in his application to the Court, contested the circumstances of his being searched at the PDFOC and alleged that no arms or other prohibited items had been found as a result of that search.
The applicant alleged that after the search at the PDFOC he was taken to another room where a police officer produced a baton, saying that it had been found in his car.
The applicant alleged that he denied that the baton belonged to him or that it had ever been in his car.
The applicant alleged that police officers persuaded him to admit that the baton had been found during his personal search, saying that he, as a member of the Hunters' Union, was allowed to own it.

The applicant alleged that police officers threatened that if he refused to confess, they would record that the baton had been found during the personal search of A.Sis. and V.K., who, not being members of the Hunters' Union, would be prosecuted.
The applicant alleged that under such circumstances he was compelled to confess that the baton belonged to him.
The applicant alleged that only after his compelled confession were the two attesting witnesses called in and a record of his personal search drawn up.
A statement was taken from the applicant in which he submitted that he had spent the previous night at Freedom Square at a rally in support of Mr Ter-Petrosyan.
The applicant submitted in his statement that in the morning on his way home his car had been stopped on Teryan Street by police officers who had taken him and the other passengers to the PDFOC.
The applicant alleged that no incident involving resistance or assault on police officers had ever happened upon his return to Kentron Police Station.
According to the applicant, as the car pulled up at Kentron Police Station, he got out of the car upon an order from one of the police officers and they accompanied him into the building.
According to the applicant, the only thing he said when he got out of the car was to tell the police officers that his arrest was unlawful.

The applicant alleged that a number of his relatives and friends, one of his future defence lawyers and a journalist had been standing near Kentron Police Station at the time he was brought back from the forensic examination, having gathered there expecting his release.
The applicant was questioned as a suspect but refused to testify or answer any questions.
The applicant declared that he was a victim of political persecution and that the charge against him was trumped up.
The applicant declared before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan that the case against him was politically motivated.
On 1 March 2008 in the early morning a police operation was conducted on Freedom Square where several hundred demonstrators were camping.
As a result of the police operation on 1 March 2008, Freedom Square was cleared of all demonstrators, resulting in clashes between the demonstrators and the police.

On 1 March 2008 criminal proceedings were instituted regarding the events at Freedom Square on the grounds that the leaders of the opposition and their supporters had organised unlawful demonstrations, incited disobedience and committed violence against the police.
Following the events of 1-2 March 2008, a state of emergency was declared by the President of Armenia.

On 2 March 2008 another set of criminal proceedings was instituted on the grounds that the leaders of the opposition and their supporters had organised mass disorder in the streets of Yerevan, including murders, violence and other reprehensible acts.
The decision to join the applicant's criminal case to case no. 62202608 stated that the applicant had also taken part in organising and conducting the unlawful demonstrations.

The investigator's application to extend detention stated that sufficient information had been obtained suggesting that the applicant, after the defeat of Mr Ter-Petrosyan in the presidential election, having joined a group of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's like-minded followers and conspired with them to usurp State power in violation of Armenia's Constitution, had actively participated in the implementation of the mentioned criminal plan.

In the application to extend the applicant's detention on 15 June 2008, the investigator added that, following a number of investigative measures, no sufficient evidence had been obtained directly implicating the applicant in the commission of the criminal act investigated in case no. 62202608.

On 19 June 2008 the General Prosecutor's Office wrote to the investigator dealing with the applicant's case, drawing his attention to the fact that the applicant had been charged only under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The General Prosecutor's Office noted that the applicant's actions had also contained elements of an offence envisaged by Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code (illegal carrying of a cold weapon) and instructed the investigator to bring new charges.
On 26 June 2008 the investigator decided to bring a new charge against the applicant under Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
The applicant pleaded not guilty and contested the factual allegations against him at trial.
The applicant lodged several requests with the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan seeking to call witnesses on his behalf.
The applicant requested that a number of persons be summoned as witnesses, including S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y., who were his relatives, political supporters and one journalist.

The applicant submitted that S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y. had gathered at Kentron Police Station and had been standing at the entrance when he was brought back by police officers from the forensic examination and could confirm that no incident had taken place as he left the car and entered the police building.
The applicant requested that A.Sis. and V.K., who had been kept at Kentron Police Station on the night from 24 to 25 February 2008, be summoned as witnesses.

The applicant submitted that A.Sis. and V.K. had witnessed from their cell window how he had been escorted into the police building and later had heard no shouts or sounds of protest when he had been escorted through the lobby inside the building.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request to summon S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y. on the ground that the case file contained no information about those persons.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request to summon A.Sis. and V.K. on the ground that it was not necessary to call those persons since the materials of the case contained sufficient information to draw appropriate conclusions.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant's arguments and the materials submitted by him to be unreliable, in conflict with the circumstances of the case and provided by persons who had close relations with the applicant, were not impartial and aimed to protect him.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had failed to assess properly the evidence and ignored his submissions in support of his innocence.
In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had based its findings solely on the statements of police officers.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had refused to hear the persons whom he had sought to call as witnesses on his behalf.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had deprived him of the opportunity to question witnesses against him, namely police officers S.H. and A.H.

In his appeal of 9 December 2008, the applicant alleged that the true reason for his prosecution and conviction was his being an opposition activist and to prevent his participation in the opposition demonstrations, arguing that he had been discriminated against on the basis of his political views.

The Criminal Court of Appeal found that the arguments relied on in the applicant's appeal, including the impossibility to question in court police officers S.H. and A.H., could not serve as a valid ground for quashing the judgment as they were not indicative of a substantial violation of the criminal process.

The Criminal Court of Appeal found that the applicant's allegations that the true reason for his prosecution was his political activism and participation in the opposition demonstrations were unsubstantiated, as the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had been guided by the law, legal awareness, inner conviction and the evidence obtained and examined in court.

On 15 April 2008 the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) Committee on the Honouring of Obligations and Commitments by Member States of the Council of Europe produced the Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579).

The Explanatory Memorandum to the PACE Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that the opposition received a boost in support when a number of high-level state officials publicly denounced the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election as fraudulent and announced their support for Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the PACE Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that those officials who denounced the election were subsequently dismissed from their positions.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the PACE Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that a number of those officials, as well as several opposition activists, were arrested on seemingly artificial charges, which left the impression that their prosecution was politically motivated.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the PACE Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that according to the Helsinki Association of Armenia, a total of 14 persons were arrested and placed under investigation in the period from 20 to 29 February 2008.

Between April 2008 and June 2009 the OSCE/ODIHR (Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe/Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights) conducted a monitoring project of about a hundred trials of opposition leaders and supporters related to the events of 1-2 March 2008.
The OSCE/ODIHR monitoring project of trials related to the events of 1-2 March 2008 included the applicant's case under number 88.
